01Station Utilization & Demand Analysis

This section examines how charging demand distributes across the network's 20 stations and 2 location types, revealing where capacity constraints are most acute.

Demand by Location Type

Highway stations carry the highest average demand score (53.4), consistent with higher traffic flow and denser EV populations in those areas. The session split between location types is roughly even, but demand intensity varies significantly.

Top Stations by Demand

The top-10 stations by average charging demand are color-coded by location type. Concentrated utilization hotspots at these stations warrant capacity review.

Demand by Time Slot × Location Type

Peak time slots see demand scores substantially higher than Off-Peak across all location types, with Highway stations experiencing the steepest Peak-vs-Off-Peak differential.

Takeaway: Highway stations during Peak hours are the primary demand concentration points. Capacity expansion or load-shifting incentives should target this segment first.

02Queue Length & Waiting Time Analysis

Waiting time is the most visible customer-experience metric. This section maps bottleneck patterns across time, location, and vehicle characteristics.

Wait Time Heatmap: Time Slot × Location Type

The highest average wait (9.6 min) occurs during Off-Peak at Highway stations. The shortest average wait (9.3 min) is during Peak at Urban stations.

03Energy Consumption & Grid Load Patterns

Understanding how energy demand and grid load vary across time helps identify stress periods and optimize capacity allocation.

Station Load by Time Slot & Day of Week

Peak time slots show the highest average station load at 84.1 kW, compared to 34.7 kW during Off-Peak. Weekday loads are generally consistent, with minor day-to-day variation.

04Renewable Energy Integration & Dynamic Pricing

Maximizing renewable energy utilization is both a sustainability imperative and an economic opportunity. This section examines when and where green charging is most achievable, and how pricing signals align with grid conditions.

Renewable Ratio by Weather & Time Slot

Clear conditions yield the highest renewable penetration (0.357), while Cloudy conditions drop to 0.351. Off-Peak periods average 0.393, suggesting time-of-use alignment can boost green charging.

Renewable Ratio Heatmap: Weather × Time Slot

Electricity Price vs Renewable Ratio

The correlation between electricity price and renewable ratio is r = -0.005, indicating that higher renewable availability tends to coincide with lower prices. This creates a natural incentive for price-sensitive charging during green windows.

Takeaway: Clear conditions during Off-Peak hours offer the highest renewable ratio (39.3%). Pricing incentives that encourage charging during these windows would simultaneously improve sustainability metrics and reduce per-session energy costs.

06Optimization Insights & Recommendations

The optimization reward metric serves as a composite signal: positive values indicate sessions that were well-scheduled, loaded the grid efficiently, and aligned with renewable availability. Negative values flag sessions that stressed the grid, incurred high costs, or missed green-charging windows.

Optimization Reward by Segment

Reward Analysis

Urban stations achieve the best average optimization reward (-11.63), while Peak time slots drag the network average down (-19.80). High-priority sessions yield higher optimization rewards than low-priority ones, suggesting effective priority scheduling.

Actionable Recommendations

Load Balancing

Shift Peak Demand to Off-Peak Windows

Peak-period station loads are 2.4× higher than Off-Peak. Introduce time-of-use pricing with a 20-30% discount for Off-Peak charging to flatten the load curve. Target Highway stations first, where the Peak-vs-Off-Peak demand differential is largest.

Queue Management

Deploy Reservation & Priority Fast-Charging at Bottleneck Stations

1.3% of sessions exceed 20-minute waits. Implement slot reservations during Peak hours at the top-5 highest-demand stations. Reserve dedicated fast-chargers for high-priority vehicles (Buses, Trucks) to reduce queue blockage from long-duration sessions.

Renewable Maximization

Align Incentives with High-Renewable Windows

Clear conditions during Off-Peak hours yield 39.3% renewable ratio vs. 35.1% in the worst conditions. Offer a "Green Charge" pricing tier (10-15% discount) during renewable-rich periods to shift environmentally-conscious drivers. Display real-time renewable % at stations to influence behavior.

Pricing Strategy

Differentiate Pricing by Location Type & Vehicle Impact

Highway stations with high demand and long queues justify premium Peak pricing to fund expansion and moderate demand. Simultaneously, introduce vehicle-type-aware pricing: longer-duration vehicles (Bus, Truck) at a marginally higher rate during Peak to reflect their disproportionate grid impact, offset by Off-Peak discounts.
